name: Release Impact & Metrics
title: Clearer release notes for every update
summary: What's New entries now show who a release actually benefits — customers, businesses, or the platform — right alongside the change list.

features: Every update on the What's New page now includes a short 'Who Benefits' section explaining what changed for customers, businesses and the platform.

impact.customers: No visible change to how the app works, but What's New entries are now easier to skim — you can see at a glance who a release was for.
impact.businesses: Vendors reading What's New can now tell whether an update affects how they run their storefront, without reading the full technical list.
impact.platform: Release notes are more accountable: every release now carries a quantitative scorecard (features/improvements/fixes/etc.) for internal reporting, alongside the existing public change lists.

technicalChangelog: releases/schema.md, releases/template.json: added public `impact.{customers,businesses,platform}` block and internal-only `internal.metrics.{featuresAdded,improvements,bugFixes,performanceImprovements,securityUpdates,breakingChanges}` block.

release.service.js: normalize() defaults both new blocks defensively; toPublic() required no change since it already spreads unknown top-level keys through (impact) and only ever strips the whole `internal` key (metrics stays server-side).
whats-new.js / whats-new.html: renderImpact() renders a 'Who Benefits' section per release card when any impact field is non-empty; added .g-impact/.impact-grid/.impact-row CSS.
scripts/new-release.js: no code change needed — it already spreads the full template.json into new drafts, so impact/metrics scaffold automatically (verified with a throwaway test release).
releases/1.0.0-digital-identity.json: backfilled impact + metrics so the existing release stays schema-valid.
docs/RELEASE_MANAGEMENT.md: documented both new fields and the audience/visibility rules.
featureList: Internal-only `metrics` scorecard block on every release file.
improvementList: Release schema is additive and defensively defaulted — existing release files and the scaffolder needed zero breaking changes.
internal.migrationNotes: None. File-based, git-tracked release registry only — no database schema touched. Existing release files remain valid; new fields default to empty/zero when absent.
internal.rollbackNotes: Revert release.service.js, whats-new.js, whats-new.html. The impact/metrics keys in releases/*.json are simply ignored by the reverted code (older normalize() already drops unknown keys via explicit field mapping) — no data cleanup needed.
